newsitem.title: INDIA: Strike cripples life in Calcutta.
newsitem.headline: Strike cripples life in Calcutta.

text.p: A one-day strike by the opposition Congress party against the local communist government paralysed activity in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta on Friday.
Shops, schools and businesses closed during the strike against the alleged misuse of state funds by the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), which has governed West Bengal state for two decades.
The strike was generally peaceful barring one or two incidents of violence, state police said.

Deputy police chief Prasun Mukherjee told reporters police fired two rounds in the air to disperse a crowd that attacked a police party with bombs and stones. One police officer was injured in the incident which occured 12 km (20 miles) from Calcutta.
The situation was under control, he said.

Few government offices were operating. Some buses and trams were running in the state capital Calcutta, but there were few passengers and the city's underground railway was deserted. Bangladesh Biman and Druk Airways of Bhutan cancelled their Calcutta-bound flights.
However the Calcutta Stock Exchange was open.
Congress called the general strike to demand an inquiry by the Central Bureau of Investigation, the federal police agency, into the alleged embezzlement of government funds.
West Bengal is home to the world's oldest democratically elected communist government which completed 20 years in power last month.
The strike coincided with a nationwide bank stoppage that crippled banking operations across India.
Bank unions were protesting against government plans to allow private banks to operate in rural areas, a move they say would hurt state-run banks.
The unions were also demanding higher wages for employees in rural banks and a pension scheme for employees in private banks.
